item.title: Past Accomplishments and Future Challenges within Supply Chain Management Research
item.content:encoded:
Jessica L. Darby, Auburn University

Rebekah (Bekki) Brau, Brigham Young University

David J. Ketchen, Auburn University

This annual special issue invites authors to submit proposals for integrative literature reviews of important supply chain management research streams. The special issue aims to synthesize current knowledge and provide direction for future development in the field. Rather than submitting full papers, authors propose a review project that outlines how they will examine and synthesize a focused area of SCM scholarship.

Proposals are evaluated on their significance, feasibility, potential breadth of interest, clarity, and contribution to future research directions. The review should address a notable gap in existing literature or provide substantial new perspective beyond prior reviews. The guest editors emphasize that proposals must be carefully crafted and authors should seek colleague feedback before submission, as rough drafts will not be pre-screened.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Logistics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Integrative reviews of supply chain management research that focus on a specific topic or apply a particular theory across different topics
  • Research streams in supply chain management that require scholarly review
  • Significant SCM research areas with limited recent published reviews or novel contributions beyond existing reviews
  • Supply chain management topics of broad interest across specialty areas and neighboring fields
